Class ColumnBatch

java.lang.Object
dev.hardwood.writer.ColumnBatch
public final class ColumnBatch extends Object

One aligned slice of a file's columns. Every column in a batch must have the same number of values, which is the batch's row count.

A batch is not constructed directly: ParquetFileWriter.writeBatch(Consumer) creates it, bound to the schema, hands it to a filler that populates the columns, then submits it — so there is no separate build or submit step to forget. Columns are addressed by index or by name, and the schema binding lets every identifier be validated as it is added — an unknown name, an out-of-range index, a non-INT32 column, or setting the same column twice (whether by index or name) all fail eagerly rather than at write time.

writer.writeBatch(b -> b
        .ints(0, idColumn)
        .ints("value", valueColumn));

  • Method Details

    • ints

      public ColumnBatch ints(int columnIndex, int[] values)

      Adds the values for a REQUIRED INT32 column, addressed by index.

      The array is referenced, not copied, so it must not be mutated until the batch has been written.

      Parameters:
      columnIndex - zero-based leaf-column index
      values - the column's values for this batch
      Returns:
      this batch, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the index is out of range, the column is already set, or the length does not match the other columns in this batch

    • ints

      public ColumnBatch ints(String columnName, int[] values)

      Adds the values for a REQUIRED INT32 column, addressed by name.

      The array is referenced, not copied, so it must not be mutated until the batch has been written.

      Parameters:
      columnName - the column's name
      values - the column's values for this batch
      Returns:
      this batch, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if no column has that name, the column is already set (by name or index), or the length does not match the other columns
